findings.title: Elysium's only block producer and a public Arbitrum One node run go1.25.12, which lacks the go1.25.13 prove and stack slot merging fixes, and no EVM result was found to depend on them
findings.difference: Ethereum clients are not tied to one build, and the go-ethereum releases are built with a supported Go toolchain. Elysium has a single sequencer whose build reports go1.25.12, and the PublicNode Arbitrum One node reports go1.25.12 as well. Between the go1.25.12 and go1.25.13 tags, 25 files of src/cmd/compile and src/cmd/internal differ (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-11-27). Two of the changes reach amd64. First, prove.go replaces addLocalFacts with a walk that first sorts each block's values topologically (topoSortValuesInBlock) and then folds the arguments of each value before it adds the facts that value teaches (constantFoldArguments, addValueFact). This is the backport of Go issue 80517 (issue 80618, CLs 807221 and 807222, "fix time traveling proofs in prove"), in which a fact learned from a later value was used to simplify an earlier one and the amd64 reproducer made an indirect call to an attacker-chosen address. Second, liveness/mergelocals.go stops merging the stack slots of two address-taken locals when an op may carry the address into its result (Go issue 80127, backport 80477). The new addrSinkArg flags are set on amd64 ops as well, although the reported failure was on riscv64. The other changes are riscv64 sign extension in regalloc (issue 80578), mips and mips64 fixes and DWARF output. go1.27.3 already carries the topological prove walk (go1.27.3 prove.go line 1705).
findings.mechanism: A wrong proof in the prove pass removes a branch or a bounds check, or marks a shift as bounded. On amd64 a 64 bit shift instruction uses only the low six bits of its count, so a shift the compiler wrongly believes bounded would turn a shift by 64 or more into a shift by the count modulo 64. In the integer library the limb shifts of Lsh, Rsh and SRsh, the normalisation shift of udivrem and the branch on the shift count in opSHL, opSHR and opSAR are the places where this would change a word. A wrong word from SHR or SAR would change TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:142-190) and BitMath (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-45), which TickBitmap uses to find the next initialised tick, and a wrong MULMOD or DIV would change FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48) and every amount computed from it. A merged stack slot would mix two local arrays, for instance the quotient and the normalised operands of udivremKnuth. Either fault would make the sequencer write a state that differs from the source. No such difference was seen: 30,222 vectors built for these branch sites, the 99,985 battery vectors, the 85,544 targeted vectors, 550 PoolManager scripts and the 23 multi-transaction scenarios give the reference result on both go1.25.12 builds. Building a go1.25.12 compiler to compare its output was not done, because the review does not allow installing a toolchain.
findings.impact: None found. A miscompile in Elysium's producer would apply to every pool there, because no other party produces blocks and the rollup accepts assertions from one whitelisted validator (cycle 13). On Arbitrum One a wrong PublicNode result would mislead only its own users, since blocks come from the Offchain Labs sequencer on go1.27.3.
findings.preconditions: The operator keeps the go1.25.12 build, and some input reaches a code site with the faulty shape. No such site has been shown.
findings.mitigations: Elysium's operator rebuilds with go1.25.13 or later, or with the go1.27 line. Integrators on Arbitrum One read from the Offchain Labs endpoint or compare two node builds.

findings.title: Elysium's planned core writer predeploy delivers result callbacks to the contract that sent an intent, and its address and interface are still unpublished
findings.difference: Ethereum has no system contract that calls back into user contracts. Kinetiq's docs say the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy lets a contract bind a HyperCore account, emit order intents and prefund a HYPE gas escrow, after which each HyperCore outcome is delivered back to the originating contract as an on-chain callback paid from the escrow. The read precompile will serve HyperCore orderbooks, prices, balances and positions to any contract. Both ship in an ArbOS upgrade planned for about four weeks after the 9 November mainnet launch and are not scheduled on chain.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager calls an outside address only for a native payout, a token transfer, the balanceOf read of sync and the hook calls (src/types/Currency.sol:48, src/types/Currency.sol:73, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). For the predeploy to treat the PoolManager as an originating contract, the PoolManager would have to call one of its intent or bind functions, and none of these four calls carries such a selector unless the predeploy answers transfer(address,uint256) or balanceOf(address) or sits at an address with valid hook bits. A callback into the PoolManager would reach a function by selector, and every function that moves value requires the unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:291-336). This cannot be checked further until the address and interface are published.
findings.impact: None found under the published description. If the predeploy answered transfer from the PoolManager and moved a balance, an ordinary account could use P2 to trigger it, so the call shapes must be rerun on the day the upgrade is scheduled.
findings.preconditions: Elysium's chain owner schedules the ArbOS upgrade.
findings.mitigations: Rerun the special-address call shapes of cycle 34 against the new addresses before the activation time, and read the predeploy source.

leadResults.answer: Run on all four endpoints the lead names. arb1: 137 of 137 calls equal; rh: 137 of 137 calls equal; ely: 137 of 137 calls equal; pubnode: 137 of 137 calls equal, each scenario in one blockStateCall with up to 19 transactions and its own web3_clientVersion bracket; Robinhood Chain answered from both architectures. stalesync.py gives zero slots in the next transaction and the synced values in the same transaction on all four, and the three borrow scripts return the reference bytes on all four. No transient value passes between transactions.

The compiled output was not inspected: building a go1.25.12 compiler in the sandbox was refused under the review's no-install rule, and no go1.25.12 binary is present (only go1.24.7 and go1.25.1). The source was compared instead. Between the go1.25.12 and go1.25.13 tags, 25 files of src/cmd/compile and src/cmd/internal differ (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched 2026-11-27). Two of the changes reach amd64. First, prove.go replaces addLocalFacts with a walk that first sorts each block's values topologically (topoSortValuesInBlock) and then folds the arguments of each value before it adds the facts that value teaches (constantFoldArguments, addValueFact). Second, liveness/mergelocals.go stops merging the stack slots of two address-taken locals when an op may carry the address into its result (Go issue 80127, backport 80477). The new addrSinkArg flags are set on amd64 ops as well, although the reported failure was on riscv64. The other changes are riscv64 sign extension in regalloc (issue 80578), mips and mips64 fixes and DWARF output. go1.27.3 already carries the topological prove walk (go1.27.3 prove.go line 1705). The 30,222 vectors aimed at the shift-count branches and the multi-limb division paths match on Elysium and the PublicNode go1.25.12 build, as do the battery, the targeted set, the scripts and the scenarios. No wrong word was found, so the residual risk is recorded under F-136 (operator, info).
